newsitem.title: UK: DIARY - Today in Westminster - Jan 15.
newsitem.headline: DIARY - Today in Westminster - Jan 15.

text.p: The following are expected to be the main events in Britain's Parliament on Wednesday.
- Remaining stages of the Crime and Punishment (Scotland) Bill.
- Foreign Affairs Committee publishes a report on the development of UK interests and links in Latin America, 1100 GMT. News conference then in Committee Room 8.
- Trade and Industry Committee hears evidence on energy regulation from Eastern Group (1030 GMT), Scottish Power (1110 GMT) and Director General of Water Services (1150 GMT).
- Social Security minister Alistair Burt gives evidence to the Social Security Committee on unfunded pension liabilities in the European Union, 1615 GMT.
- Transport Secretary Sir George Young gives evidence on the transport expenditure settlement to the Transport Committee, 1600 GMT.
- Selection Committee meets to decide composition of the Finance Bill Committee.
- Lords European Communities Sub-Committee A (Economic and Finacial Affairs, Trade and External Relations) hears evidence from Arlene McCarthy MEP 1145 GMT.
INDICT, all-party campaign to indict Iraqi war criminals, is launched. Chaired by Labour's Ann Clwyd. (1100 GMT).
LONDON - Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind and Trade and Industry Secretary Ian Lang launches "Open for Business in Central Europe" export promotion campaign. (1100 GMT).
